schema.label: Spend over £500
schema.one_row_is: one payment line as published in a body's transparency return

columns.name: body
columns.meaning: the paying body, as the index names the publisher

columns.name: threshold_gbp
columns.meaning: the return's stated threshold: 500 or 250. Carried on every row because thresholds differ between bodies and a combined table must not imply one

columns.name: payment_date
columns.meaning: ISO date; null if the source gives only a period

columns.name: period
columns.meaning: the return's period label (e.g. '2024-25 Q1', 'April 2024') as published

columns.name: supplier
columns.meaning: supplier name exactly as published — never normalised, never matched to another body's spelling by this family

columns.name: amount_gbp
columns.meaning: the published amount; sign preserved (credits are negative if published so)

rules: Supplier names are published text. Grouping two spellings as one supplier is an eyeballed decision made elsewhere, never here.
The threshold is read from the dataset title or the return's own header, and stored per row.
Amounts below the stated threshold are kept if the source published them; the threshold describes the return, not a filter we apply.
A VAT column, where present, is kept as published in 'description' context, not added to or subtracted from the amount.
Personal names appearing as suppliers are kept as published: the body published them under the transparency code.
